name: Hòn Tre Cable Car
kicker: The cable crossing to Hòn Tre
summary: Sea cable to Hòn Tre: ride the 3,320 m crossing for a day on the bay’s largest island. It opened in March 2007 as the longest sea crossing then, and it is also the longest cable in Southeast Asia. Swim, snorkel, or jet-ski once you are across. Cabins run 8:30–23:00 both ways.
getThere: The shore station on the city side of the bay.
heroCaption: A cabin on the cable, with Hòn Tre and the Vinpearl hillside across the water

notice.title: Two rankings, one cable
notice.body: The cable is 3,320 m. At the March 2007 opening it was the longest sea crossing, and it is also the longest cable in Southeast Asia.

body: Hòn Tre is the large island in the bay, about 3,000 to 3,323 ha, and 5 km from Nha Trang. The cable is 3,320 m, inaugurated in March 2007. Swim, snorkel, or jet-ski once you are across. The amusement park on the island is the same visit as the crossing, reached by this cable.

Vinpearl Harbour opened on 26 January 2024 on Hòn Tre in Vĩnh Nguyên. Cable hours run both ways from 8:30 to 23:00, and ticket sales stop at 22:30. From 23:00 until 02:00 a speedboat runs back to shore, with the last shore boat at 02:15.

figures.caption: The cable and the island from the same crossing
figures.alt: Another frame of the Hòn Tre cable over the bay

gettingThere: You reach Hòn Tre by the 3,320 m cable from the city shore, or by boat after the cable hours. A free bus runs from the airport to the Hòn Tre pier.

legs.heading: From Trần Phú
legs.body: Ride to the shore station, then take the cable. The crossing is 3,320 m.

legs.heading: From the airport
legs.body: A free bus runs from the airport to the Hòn Tre pier.

hours: Cable both ways 8:30–23:00. Ticket sales stop at 22:30. Last shore boat 02:15.
admissionNote: The cable ticket is separate. The bay scenic fee for the Hòn Tre route is 8,000 VND a person each crossing, plus 3,000 VND at the pier. Children under 6 and Khánh Hòa residents are among those exempt. A child from 6 to under 16 pays half.
